Pay for GPU infrastructure, not per-token usage. Costs scale predictably with your own capacity.
Training data, prompts, and outputs stay in your infrastructure. No provider data retention or review.

sec-head.h2: Hugging Face vs OpenAI for custom models?

p: The difference between Hugging Face and OpenAI for custom models is a build versus buy decision. Hugging Face open weights give you self-serve fine-tuning and complete control over custom model hosting — your VPC, on-premises, or a dedicated GPU cluster — with full data ownership and no per-token fees. OpenAI delivers powerful managed APIs with convenient fine-tuning endpoints, but locks you into closed weights, per-token costs, and provider-controlled infrastructure. Building on Hugging Face wins when you need tailored behavior, strict data privacy, or predictable cost at scale; buying OpenAI wins when you prioritize velocity and zero infrastructure maintenance.

sec-head.h2: Hugging Face open weights vs OpenAI API

td: Download open weights and fine-tune with LoRA, QLoRA, or full fine-tuning. You control the architecture, dataset splits, and evaluation loop.
Limited to OpenAI's fine-tuning API surface. No access to weights, logits, or internal model representations.
Predictable GPU infrastructure costs with zero per-token fees. Models are free to download; you pay only for compute.
Per-token charges on every inference call plus separate training fees. Costs grow linearly with usage and scale.
Self-host in your VPC or on-premises. Training data, prompts, and outputs never leave your infrastructure.
Prompts and outputs traverse OpenAI's API and are subject to their retention and safety-review policies.
Deploy to any GPU cloud, your own data center, or edge devices. No vendor approval or API keys required.
Deploy on OpenAI's cloud only. No air-gapped, VPC, or on-premises option for their closed models.

p: With open weights, every layer from tokenizer to deployment checkpoint is inspectable and modifiable, so your roadmap is never blocked by a vendor's release schedule. Buying API access trades this leverage for convenience, leaving custom model decisions in the hands of a provider.
